newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Telstra sees soft revenue growth in 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Telstra sees soft revenue growth in 2nd half.

text.p: Australian government owned telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp AOT.AX said on Friday it expected soft revenue growth in the second half of its year to June 30, with growth similar to that in the first half.
"We are still seeing soft revenue growth but it will still be around the level we experienced in the first half," Telstra chief executive officer Frank Blount told a news conference.
Telstra reported a 4.6 percent rise in sales to A$7.77 billion in the six months ended December 31.
Blount said Telstra's first half revenue was under pressure from a slowing economy and increased competition. Australia's telecommunications industry is to be fully deregulated mid-1997.
"As you know we had 100 percent of the market, so we know we are going to lose market share," Blount said.

"But the good news is, the strategy of going after the value chain is beginning to work very well. We have more than enough revenue growth from there to offset the declines in those traditional businesses," Blount said.
Telstra has started pay television and Internet operations over the past two years to add to its telephony business, where it had a market monopoly on local calls until last year.
Its monopoly on long distance calls ended in 1992.

Telstra earlier reported that its net profit before abormals rose 16.1 percent to A$1.4 billion in the six months ended December 31, 1996, while net profit after abnormals fell to A$742 million from A$1.205 billion
